review_of_specific_points.symmetry_requirement_Q_R_P0: Justified as an input check, but the implementer's stated reason was factually wrong. jnp.linalg.cholesky (jax 0.7.2) has symmetrize_input=True by default and uses (A+A^T)/2, i.e. it does NOT read only the lower triangle. The check is still justified: Q, R, P0 are covariances (symmetric by definition) and upstream uses them inconsistently when asymmetric: simulate_lgssm only via Cholesky (=> effectively (Q+Q^T)/2; demonstrated by test_upstream_cholesky_symmetrises_rationale: asymmetric Q equals symmetrised Q to 1e-14 and differs from the lower-triangle reading), while kf adds Q unsymmetrised in F P F^T + Q. Tolerance rtol=1e-10, atol=1e-12 accepts float round-off asymmetry. REPAIRED: error message now states the correct rationale.
review_of_specific_points.post_hoc_non_finite_checks: Justified, no recomputation: upstream returns NaN silently (no exception) when a Cholesky fails (non-PD innovation covariance in kf, singular predictive covariance in rts via cho_factor, non-PD Q/R/P0 in simulate_lgssm); demonstrated by direct upstream calls in test_rationale_upstream_silent_failures and test_nonpd_simulation_is_nan_upstream. The checks run after the upstream call on its outputs only. No positive-definiteness pre-check is imposed: a singular P0 (P0=0) and F=0,Q=0 run through kf exactly as upstream (tests), and only the smoother then errors. Minor note (not changed): a non-finite gradient raises an error even if the nll was finite; acceptable because the requested output would be invalid.
review_of_specific_points.one_d_ys_only_for_dy_1: Justified. Upstream tests/test_filters.py::test_kf itself passes 1-D ys (101,) with dy=1; the wrapper reshapes to (T+1,1) and results are bitwise equal to the executor capture for both (101,) and (101,1) inputs. For dy>1 a 1-D ys runs upstream without error but broadcasts each scalar observation to all dy components (shown by direct call), which is silently wrong, so rejecting it is correct.
